evals.prompt: Verify tutor's committed eval fixtures end to end, offline: parse the realism Export, confirm the synthetic Collections cover its gaps, confirm the fixture Briefs and Decks are well-formed with their planted flaws registered, and confirm the pinned Scryfall snapshot and the fixture Oracle derived from it cover exactly the fixture cards.
evals.expected_output: A red/green report over the fixture tree with every mechanical expectation green, proving the harness — case loading, fixture resolution, fixed-predicate grading, report emission — end to end without any network call.
expectations: The realism fixture collections/real-collection.csv parses header-keyed as CSV with exactly 577 data rows.
A synthetic Collection row carries the etched Foil value the real Export lacks.
Synthetic Collection rows carry non-English Language codes the real Export lacks, including the disputed zhs.
A synthetic Collection row carries a promo collector number (letter-suffixed or starred) the real Export lacks.
Per-Format shaped pool Collections cover Kitchen 20 (Uncharted Haven beside mono-white candidates) and Standard (playset quantities), parsing with the full ManaBox header.
Fixture Briefs parse as flat key: value Blocks with the required format: line and only canonical Brief keys.
Fixture Decks parse as ManaBox-importable Deck Blocks: title comment, Board headers, quantity lines with set-and-number pins on nonbasics.
Some fixture Decks carry planted flaws for Review evals, each registered in the manifest and naming cards present in its Deck (or absent from every Collection for availability flaws).
The pinned Scryfall snapshot covers every card the fixtures reference and nothing else, with its capture metadata on line one.
The fixture Oracle scryfall/oracle.jsonl is byte-identical to a fresh offline derivation from the pinned snapshot.

Every Oracle line is name-keyed with mana value, colors, color identity, type line, oracle text, the four sanctioned legalities, and the game_changer flag — no UUIDs, tokens excluded, basics included, multi-faced names flattened with //.
The Oracle's first line records generated_at and the source Export's newest Added watermark.
Evals never touch the network: a tripwire scan finds the literal live Scryfall API host string in no eval or fixture file except the deliberate refresh script and the snapshot's provenance metadata.

evals.prompt: Generate the Oracle for a Collection home offline: run the oracle skill's build script over the realism Export with resolution pinned to the committed Scryfall snapshot, and verify the written oracle.jsonl, the tolerant-parse report, and the Name + Set code fallback — without any network call.
evals.expected_output: oracle.jsonl beside the Export — metadata line one carrying generated_at and the source Export's newest Added watermark, then one shape-exact JSON line per unique card name — plus a report counting malformed rows skipped and cards resolved, with legality data marked informational-only.
expectations: Run offline against the pinned snapshot, the oracle script writes the Oracle beside the realism Export: line one records generated_at plus the source Export's newest Added watermark, then one line per unique card name.

Every Oracle line the script writes is byte-identical to the fixture Oracle's line for the same card — the shape-exact record with four-Format legalities, the game_changer boolean, tokens excluded, basics included, multi-faced names flattened with //, and no UUIDs.
Malformed Export rows are skipped and reported with a count and examples, and a header missing the identity columns is the only hard failure.
An Export row whose Scryfall ID the snapshot no longer knows still resolves through its Name + Set code.
Run as /tutor:oracle in a Collection home, the skill's closing report surfaces the two staleness signals and marks Scryfall legality data informational-only, without implying Scryfall endorsement.

evals.prompt: I want a new Commander deck around Tatyova, Benthic Druid — simic, lands matter, steady card draw, nothing above 6 mana, and no infinite combos. My Baylen deck can be cannibalized for it. Scripted answers for the rest of the brief conversation: name it Tatyova Landfall; power 2; yes, the Export is current; keep every other deck committed.
evals.expected_output: The brief conversation fires, asks the single Export/Oracle freshness question, and ends with a Brief Block equivalent to evals/fixtures/briefs/commander-tatyova-landfall.txt — flat key: value lines, format: commander, the mechanical ask as a constraint: line and the fuzzy asks in notes:, donor: Baylen, the Haymaker recognized from the Export's deck rows, no budget key — validated by skills/brief/scripts/validate_brief.py and written to the Collection home.
expectations: The /tutor:brief command is a thin wrapper handing off to the brief skill, whose metadata.version matches the plugin manifest's pinned version.
The brief skill's description fires from natural language: it names deck-intent triggers beyond the /tutor:brief command itself.
Every fixture Brief validates against the brief skill's validator, donors recognized from its manifest-paired Export's deck rows.
The validator holds the Power ladder: a 1-5 number with trailing free text passes and an out-of-ladder number fails.
The validator holds donor grammar: donor: all passes and an unrecognized donor Deck name fails against the Export's deck rows.
No fixture Brief declares a play variant as its format:, and the Archenemy fixture expresses the variant in play variant: with the Centerpiece naming the villain.
The freshness helper surfaces the fixture Export's newest Added and both Oracle staleness signals deterministically, and degrades gracefully when the Oracle is absent.
The brief skill's text pins the grammar it must emit: all nine canonical keys, only format required, no budget key, Power defaulting to 2, one freshness question, and a closing handoff to Build.
Invoked from natural language alone — no /tutor:brief command typed — the skill fires and opens the brief conversation.
Run with the scripted answers, the conversation ends in a Brief Block equivalent to the Tatyova fixture Brief, written to the Collection home.
Mechanical asks land as constraint: lines and fuzzy asks land in notes: — each where it can be honestly enforced.
The conversation asks the Export/Oracle freshness question exactly once.
A pasted Export is always accepted and beats the file on conflict: the diff — rows added, removed, quantities changed — is reported, then the paste is worked from.

evals.prompt: Start a Build from the fixture Tatyova Brief in a Collection home: generate the declarative Suite from the Brief and the Commander Format profile before any card is picked, and show it honestly red on the empty Deck through the fixed runner.
evals.expected_output: The committed fixture Suite — snapshotted Commander targets, the quota table over the global Role vocabulary, mechanical Brief constraints under provenance comments, an empty Role-tag section — reproduced byte-identical by the generator, plus the runner's red empty-Deck report matching the committed reference: every size, mana-base-count, curve, and quota Check red, constraint-shaped Checks vacuously green, both written to the Collection home.
expectations: The Commander Format profile is first-class declarative data: deck size 100, singleton copy limit, lands, curve, and consistency check targets, per-bracket Game Changers limits 0 / 0 / 3 / unlimited / unlimited for Power 1-5, a banlist parameter, and judgment-flavored Role guidance.
Run over the fixture Tatyova Brief, the Commander profile, and the fixture Oracle, the Suite generator reproduces the committed fixture Suite byte-identical — declarative data, never code.

The fixture Suite carries every generated Check class — Legality, Availability, Mana base, Curve, Quotas over the global Role vocabulary, mechanical Brief constraints, hypergeometric Consistency — with no budget class, targets snapshotted from the profile, Brief-set values under brief: provenance comments, and an empty roles: section because no card is picked yet.

Through the unmodified runner, the empty fixture Deck reports byte-identical to the committed reference: every size, mana-base-count, curve, and quota Check red, the singleton, color identity, banlist, Game Changers, and availability Checks vacuously green, exit code red.
The /tutor:build command is a thin wrapper handing off to the build skill, whose metadata.version matches the plugin manifest's pinned version.

The build skill's text pins the front half: the Suite and its report written to the Collection home, the offer to generate an absent Oracle via /tutor:oracle when network allows, a pasted Export or Block beating the file, a refused constraint going back to the Brief, and no card picked before the Suite exists.
Run live, /tutor:build walks a Collection home from Brief to written Suite and red report, explaining vacuous green honestly.
Role tagging judgment is recorded once per card in the Suite's roles: section as Build fills the Deck, and quota Checks count those tags mechanically.

evals.prompt: Review the fixture Tatyova Deck in a Collection home: fan out the two review axes (Standards, Brief) over the Deck, its Brief, and its Suite report, assemble the Review Block mechanically, and prove the planted Review-class flaws in the Review-flawed fixture Deck are Review territory the Suite cannot see.
evals.expected_output: A Review Block — deck: and date: reference lines, one overall verdict: line, then a standards: and a brief: section side by side, each with its own arithmetic verdict and at most five Findings worst first naming cards — written to the Collection home, closing instructions matching the Verdict, the Deck untouched.
expectations: Verdicts are arithmetic over Findings, hard-graded through the assembler: any blocker makes an axis rebuild, only notes playable, clean ship, the overall Verdict is the worst axis, a blocker past the display cap still rebuilds, and the same Findings assemble to the same bytes — no fresh judgment in aggregation.

The assembled Review Block carries deck: and date: reference lines, one overall verdict: line, then one section per axis — standards: first, brief: second, side by side, never merged or reranked — each with its own verdict and Findings naming cards.
Each axis shows at most five Findings, worst first, with a one-line summary of the rest naming its cards.

A Finding is a severity (blocker or note), named cards, the problem, and at most one suggestion — an owned swap or an unowned Maybeboard candidate; the assembler refuses a malformed Finding with exit 2 and no partial Block.
With no Brief the review runs Standards-only: the Brief axis reports no Brief available and the overall Verdict is the Standards axis alone.
The /tutor:review command is a thin wrapper handing off to the review skill, whose metadata.version matches the plugin manifest's pinned version.

The review skill pins the locked Smell baseline v1 by name: synergy island, dead card, win-more, no comeback plan, piloting overload, fragile mana, theme tax, redundancy gap, curve lie, interaction mismatch.

The Commander profile authors the per-Format review standards from the recorded seeds — politics, functional-copy redundancy, answer spread — as data the Standards axis reads, and the review skill pins that the profile overrides the baseline.

The review skill's text pins the contract: two parallel subagents, one per axis, aggregated side by side with the sequential two-pass fallback as robustness; Review trusts the green Suite and never recounts Check territory but may flag a Check target as mis-set for the Brief; Review never edits the Deck; ship closes with the ManaBox import suggestion while playable and rebuild offer a Build re-run consuming the Review Block; Power fit, mass land denial, chained extra turns, and early two-card combos are Review judgment, not Checks.

The Review-flawed fixture Deck plants only Review-territory flaws: every Check green on the clean fixture Deck stays green on it through the unmodified runner, and each registered standards/brief flaw names owned cards present in the Deck.

Run live, /tutor:review fans out the two axis subagents in parallel and aggregates their Findings side by side through the assembler, falling back to two sequential passes when subagents are unavailable.
Run live over the Review-flawed fixture Deck and its Brief, the Review's Findings catch every planted flaw the manifest registers, on the axis its class names, naming the planted cards.

Run live over a Check-flawed fixture Deck, the review routes Check territory to the Suite: the planted legality and availability flaws surface through the runner's report, never as fresh Review Findings.
Run live, fuzzy Brief asks are judged on the Brief axis, and a Check target the Brief outgrew is flagged as mis-set for the Brief without recounting the Suite.

evals.prompt: Finish the Build for the Tatyova Brief in a Collection home, as an Upgrade of the owner's existing ManaBox deck (its own rows freed by donor: lines): add and swap owned cards until the Suite is green through the fixed runner — the clean deck's Tolarian Terror breaks the Brief's 'nothing above 6 mana' cap and must be swapped for an owned, free, on-Brief card — record Role judgment in the Suite's roles: section, and ship the ManaBox-importable Deck Block to the deck library.
evals.expected_output: The committed built fixtures, byte for byte: the Upgrade Brief; the built Suite (the generated Suite plus recorded Role tags, no target bent); the shipped Deck Block — nonbasics pinned to owned printings, basics lumped last, inline category comments, the unowned wishlist entry on the Maybeboard, the Fan Content footer — and the all-green report from the unmodified runner, with contention-aware availability honoring the donor: lines.
expectations: The Upgrade Brief validates against the Export and frees the target Deck's own rows through a donor: line — the rename case in action: automatic freeing keys on name identity, and the ManaBox deck's name matches neither the Brief's name: nor the Block's title, so the human's donor: line connects the two names.
Every card in the built Deck is drawn from the Collection fixture: contention-aware availability over the Export's deck rows reports every copy free under the Brief's donor: lines.
Declined contention is reported in the honest sentence shape: a want whose copies are all committed to a Deck the Brief never freed comes back as 'wanted <card>; all copies committed to <deck>'.
Format legality holds and the Suite re-runs through the fixed runner: the built Suite over the shipped Deck Block reproduces the committed all-green report byte-identical, exit green.
Build never bends targets: the built Suite differs from a fresh generation over the Upgrade Brief only by the Role tags recorded in its roles: section.

The shipped Deck Block parses as ManaBox-importable text: '// <name>' first, reserved Board headers only for Boards in use, every nonbasic outside the Maybeboard pinned to an owned printing with set code and collector number, inline '// category' comments, basics lumped per name last in their Board after a blank line, and the short-form Fan Content footer line exactly once.
The Maybeboard is the wishlist Board: its entries carry no printing pin and may be unowned — the one place the collection-only rule bends.
Blocks survive the round-trip: re-shipping the shipped Deck Block reproduces it byte-identical, and the committed report reads the full 100 cards from it.
A Deck card missing from the Oracle degrades per-card to flagged model knowledge, never a hard failure: the runner still reports with the uncovered card named in the report head.
The pasted-Export case holds as parser-tolerance smoke: the same availability verdicts from a paste-shaped Export — BOM, CRLF line endings, extra quoting — as from the file on disk.

The build skill's text pins the back half: the loop through the fixed runner with targets never bent, contention consulted and declined contention reported out loud, the honest red ending with the human's three options, the shipped Deck Block with the Fan Content footer and the informational-only legality caveat, the Maybeboard wishlist, and closing instructions naming the Blocks Review needs.
The built Deck honors the Brief's intent: lands matter, steady card draw, nothing above 6 mana, no infinite combos, at bracket-2 power.

evals.prompt: Upgrade the Tatyova Landfall Deck in a Collection home: the human imported the shipped Deck Block into ManaBox and synced a fresh Export — its rows now committed to Tatyova Landfall — and asks for a Build re-run with the existing Deck, Suite, and Brief from the deck library, the Review Block's Findings as the work list. Prove the Upgrade is an ordinary Build re-run: nothing regenerates, and the rebuilt Deck's own copies are freed automatically.
evals.expected_output: The committed built fixtures untouched: the byte-identical Suite re-run through the unmodified runner reproduces the committed all-green report against the fresh Export, every copy the Deck needs is free with no donor: line naming the Deck itself, declined contention stays honest for every other Deck, and the build skill pins the Upgrade contract — no fourth deck verb.
expectations: A Build re-run given an existing Deck frees that Deck's own copies automatically: against a fresh Export whose deck rows commit the shipped Block's cards to the ManaBox deck its title names, contention-aware availability reports every copy free — no donor: line names the Deck itself.

The byte-identical Suite artifact re-runs against the fresh Export through the unmodified runner: nothing regenerates, the committed built Suite's bytes stay untouched, and the committed all-green report is reproduced byte-identical — the rebuilt Deck never contends with itself.
Nothing already tagged is re-tagged: the built Suite's roles: section already covers every Deck card outside the Maybeboard, so only cards new to the pool would need fresh Role tagging at an Upgrade.
Contention stays real at an Upgrade: against the fresh Export, a want whose copies sit in a Deck neither donor-named nor the Deck itself still declines in the honest sentence.

The build skill's text pins the Upgrade contract: an ordinary Build re-run with a fresh Export and the existing Deck — no fourth deck verb; the existing Suite re-run as-is, never regenerated; the rebuilt Deck's own copies freed automatically; a Review Block consumed as the work list on a playable or rebuild Verdict; and the deck library treated as a growing library whose artifacts an Upgrade updates in place.

Run live, /tutor:build recognizes an Upgrade from the existing Deck's artifacts in the deck library, re-runs the Suite as-is, tags only cards new to the pool, and consumes the Review Block's Findings as its work list — the revision loop stays manual, the human re-running Build after reading the Review.

evals.prompt: Prove Kitchen 20 is an equal-citizen Format in a Collection home: read the Kitchen 20 profile as pure data, generate the Sunlit Whiskers Suite from the fixture Brief through the unchanged engine, run the clean fixture Pack and its packet-flawed sibling over the Kitchen 20 pool through the fixed runner, and show the Format pinning Power off and authoring its per-Format review standards.
evals.expected_output: The Kitchen 20 vertical green on data alone: the committed fixture Suite reproduced byte-identical by the untouched generator, the clean Pack's all-green report and the flawed Pack's red report matching their committed references — second rare, multicolor card, and off-profile nonbasic each red on its own packet Check — no Power anywhere in the flow, and the three recorded review-standard seeds carried as profile data.
expectations: The Kitchen 20 profile ships as pure data pinned by the Foundations Beginner Box research: a 20-card mono-color Pack target, strict singleton nonlands, an 8-9 land window with Uncharted Haven the only allowed nonbasic, exactly 1 rare with rare as the ceiling, no multicolor cards, and the evergreen keyword list as profile data.

Kitchen 20 carries no Power — the profile pins power: none, the Brief validator rejects a power: line beside format: kitchen 20, the generator mirrors that rule, the committed Kitchen 20 Suite carries no power segment, and the brief skill says not to ask.

Run over the fixture Kitchen 20 Brief, the Kitchen 20 profile, and the fixture Oracle, the untouched Suite generator reproduces the committed fixture Suite byte-identical: the packet Legality Checks generate from the profile through the existing engine, with no banlist, Game Changers, color-identity, or quota Check and an empty roles: section.

Through the unmodified runner over the Kitchen 20 pool, the clean fixture Pack reports byte-identical to the committed reference: every Check green including the packet Legality Checks, exit code green — the fixture Pack pool builds green.

Through the unmodified runner, each planted packet violation goes red on its own Check — the second rare on legality.rare_count, the multicolor card on legality.mono_color, the off-profile nonbasic on legality.nonbasic_lands, the non-evergreen keyword on legality.evergreen, the 21st card on legality.size — byte-identical to the committed reference, exit code red.

The Kitchen 20 profile authors the per-Format review standards from the recorded seeds — pack-combining quality, teaching pilotability, rare-as-payoff — as data the Standards axis reads, and pack-combining quality stays review guidance, not a Check: no generated or templated Check id covers Pack combining.

evals.prompt: Build and review a Casual 60 deck in a Collection home from the fixture Casual 60 Brief over the Standard-shaped pool, and prove the thin sanctioned 60-card Formats — Standard, Modern, Pioneer — are data profiles whose legality is read per card from the Oracle's legalities: the sanctioned-legality Check goes red on a fixture card illegal in that Format.
evals.expected_output: The committed Casual 60 fixtures byte for byte — the built Suite (generated targets plus recorded Role tags), the ManaBox-importable Deck Block, the all-green report, and the assembled Review Block — plus a Standard Suite over the legality-flawed fixture Deck whose banlist Check reports red naming the illegal card, all through the unmodified generator, runner, and assembler.
expectations: The Casual 60 Format profile is first-class declarative data: deck size 60, a four-copy limit, lands, curve, and consistency check targets, quotas over the global Role vocabulary, and no banlist parameter and no Centerpiece demand — the kitchen table needs neither.

The thin sanctioned profiles — Standard, Modern, Pioneer — are the Casual 60 profile plus exactly their banlist parameter naming the Oracle legalities key the banlist Check reads per card: no other target differs, and no profile carries a hand-maintained banlist.
Power reads through the four 60-card profiles as one shared 1-5 ladder authored as data — 1 jank to 5 competitive — and a Brief with no power: line generates a Suite at the default, power 2.

The four 60-card Formats share one review-standards list: the review_standards sections of casual-60, standard, modern, and pioneer are byte-identical, authored data the Standards axis reads on top of the Smell baseline.

Run over the fixture Casual 60 Brief, the casual-60 profile, and the fixture Oracle, the Suite generator reproduces the committed built Suite up to its recorded Role tags — no target bent — and the unmodified runner reports the committed Casual 60 Deck all green byte-identical, exit green.
The committed Casual 60 Review reassembles byte-identical through the unmodified assembler: the recorded axis Findings in, the committed Review Block out, its Verdicts computed, never re-judged.

Through the unmodified runner, the sanctioned-legality Check reads the Oracle's per-card legalities: red on the legality-flawed Standard fixture Deck naming the card the Oracle marks not standard-legal, green over the all-legal Casual 60 Deck under the same Standard Suite.

Run live, /tutor:build walks the Casual 60 Brief from generated Suite to green through the same fixed scripts, and /tutor:review fans out the two axes with the shared 60-card review standards read from the Format profile.

evals.prompt: Plan and run a family Archenemy night as a Table in a Collection home: one brief conversation produces the Table Brief plus the untouched per-Deck Seat Briefs with every table-level line copied down, the Seats build sequentially in seat order with an earlier Seat's finished Deck Block counted as committed copies, the declared-Power match runs as a mechanical check, and the finished sitting is judged whole in a Table Review.
evals.expected_output: The fixture Table Brief validating as an index — table: anchor plus seat: lines, never embedding the per-Deck Briefs — whose seat deck names join the two Seat Briefs; the copy-down and declared-Power checks green over the good fixtures and red over the mismatched fixture; the availability and pin arithmetic declining a table-mate's committed copies in the honest sentence; and a Table Review Block — table:/date: lines, one overall verdict:, three axis sections whose findings name Seats and cards — assembled mechanically.
expectations: The fixture Table Brief is recognized by its table: anchor plus seat: lines and validates as an index: seat grammar 'seat: [role —] <deck name>[, power N]' parsed with commas kept in the deck name, two Seats minimum held, and per-Deck keys refused as embedding.

One brief conversation's artifacts hold together: every seat: deck name joins its per-Deck Brief's name: line, each Seat's Brief is an untouched valid Brief on its own, and the table-level power, constraints, play variant, and donors are copied into every Seat's Brief.

The declared-Power match is a mechanical check: every Seat's effective Power equals the table's unless its seat line overrides — green over the fixture Table with its Seat Briefs, red over the mismatched fixture naming the Seat.
Kitchen 20 Seats carry no Power: a Kitchen 20 Table Brief carrying a power: line or a seat-line override is refused.

Seat order = build order = contention priority: an earlier Seat's finished Deck Block counts as committed copies — the same want free before that Seat finishes is declined after it in the honest sentence naming the table-mate.
Table-mates are never Donor Decks: no donor: line — not even donor: all — frees a table-mate's copies, and a Table Brief donor: naming a Seat's deck is refused.
Printing pins respect the sitting: the ship script spills to the printing a table-mate left free and refuses when the table-mate holds every copy.

The Table Review Block is assembled mechanically: table: and date: reference lines, one overall verdict: line, the three axis sections — power spread, play patterns, contention fallout — side by side with the Deck Review's verdict arithmetic, findings naming Seats and cards, at most five per axis worst first, malformed Findings refused with exit 2 and no partial Block.

The skills pin the Tables loop: one brief conversation producing a Table Brief plus N untouched per-Deck Briefs (two Seats minimum), Seats building sequentially through the unchanged build loop with table-mate Blocks as committed copies, one Seat's later Upgrade carrying the Table Brief and table-mate Deck Blocks, reallocation as a human re-brief loop, and the Table Review after the last Seat.

Run live, one brief conversation for a family Archenemy night settles the whole sitting: the Table Brief and every Seat's Brief written to the Collection home, table-level lines copied down, seat order settled out loud.
Run live, the Seats build sequentially in seat order through /tutor:build, each later Seat consulting every earlier finished Deck Block as a table-mate, declined table contention reported out loud.

Run live after the last Seat, /tutor:review judges the sitting as a whole — power spread, play patterns, contention fallout — and assembles the Table Review Block through the assembler, findings naming Seats and cards.
